title: Linear-t min-entropy lower bound for non-malleable extractors
summary: Determine whether security against t related seeds forces the conjectured min-entropy lower bound for every one-bit non-malleable extractor.

formal_statement.body: Let $\mathrm{nmExt}:\{0,1\}^n\times\{0,1\}^d\to\{0,1\}$ be a $(k,\varepsilon)$-$t$-non-malleable extractor in the source model, with $\varepsilon$ in the stated small-error regime. Prove that every such extractor satisfies $k\ge \log d+2\log(1/\varepsilon)+t-O(1)$, where the additive constant is absolute, or construct an admissible infinite family that violates the linear dependence on $t$.

scope.domain: One-bit non-malleable extractors secure against t adversarially related seeds
assumptions: $\varepsilon$ lies in the source's small-error regime
The extractor output is one bit
The lower bound is interpreted up to an absolute additive constant
scope.unresolved_remainder: No inspected later work proves the full lower bound with its linear t term for every admissible one-bit t-non-malleable extractor or supplies a counterexample family.

progress.summary: The source conjectures the displayed min-entropy lower bound and explicitly leaves its linear dependence on the tampering count open.
